findings.title: Error IDs may be paired with the wrong nodestore payload
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. The returned mapping is keyed by node id, and nothing guarantees its iteration order matches the input list (backends may batch/dedupe, and missing entries are filtered out *after* the zip pairing, so one missing/reordered node shifts every subsequent pair). The result is `ErrorEvent.id` values attached to a different event's title/message/timestamp, producing incorrect summaries. Iterate `node_ids` explicitly and look up `events[node_id]` keyed by its corresponding error id.

findings.title: New table visualization path renders a permanently empty table
findings.body: When the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature is enabled, `TableWidgetVisualization` is rendered with `columns={[]}` and hard-coded empty `tableData` (`data: []`, `meta.fields: {}`), completely ignoring the `result`/`fields`/`result.meta` that `StyledSimpleTableChart` receives in the non-flagged branch. Any org with the flag on will see blank table widgets instead of their data. The real result/meta must be mapped into `TabularData`.

findings.title: get_environment_info fetches a recommended event per issue
findings.body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` and then `get_environment()` for each of the top issues while building a PR comment. This performs a Snuba/nodestore lookup plus an environment query per issue inside a loop in the comment workflow, adding several round trips to every merged-PR comment task and silently swallowing all failures. Consider resolving environments in bulk or reusing data already fetched for the top-issues query.

findings.title: Shared slow-condition map is keyed only by dcg_ids, risking KeyError
findings.body: `dcg_to_slow_conditions` is now computed once from `event_data.dcg_ids` and passed to both `get_condition_query_groups` and `get_groups_to_fire`. Previously `get_condition_query_groups` built its map from `event_data.dcg_to_groups.keys()`. If those two sets ever differ (a DCG present in `dcg_to_groups` but not in `dcg_ids`), `dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id]` raises KeyError and the whole delayed-workflow batch fails. Use a `defaultdict(list)`/`.get(dcg.id, [])` or compute the map from the union of both id sources.

findings.title: Reports with neither `age` nor `timestamp` are accepted
findings.body: Both `age` and `timestamp` are `required=False`, and DRF only runs `validate_age`/`validate_timestamp` when the field is present. A report containing neither field therefore validates successfully, even though the spec requires exactly one. Add an object-level `validate()` that rejects the both-absent case so the metric isn't recorded for unusable payloads.

findings.title: Analytics recorded before feature/permission gate
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble")` check, so every rejected (404) request is counted as an assemble event. This inflates the metric with requests that never assemble anything; move the record call after the feature check.

findings.title: TabularColumn.name typed as the field-key union prevents custom display names
findings.body: `TabularColumn<TFields>` declares `name: TFields`, the same union as `key`. Since a documented purpose of the prop is "custom display names for columns" (see tableWidgetVisualization docs/stories), arbitrary labels like `'Count of Span Duration'` will not type-check against a constrained `TFields`. `name` should be `string`.
